title: Schematic closure gives a Cartesian refining compactification triangle
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X,V,\overline X,Y,\overline Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $j:X\hookrightarrow V$, $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ be open immersions and let $q:V\to Y$, $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$ be proper with $pb=iq$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Do not assume this square Cartesian. Let $a:W\hookrightarrow\overline X$ be the scheme-theoretic closure of the open $bj(X)$, namely its smallest closed subscheme containing $X$ [sk-lem-nagata-sketch-closure], and let $W_Y=W\times_{\overline Y}Y$ with projections $b':W_Y\hookrightarrow W$, $q':W_Y\to Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. There are a quasi-compact open immersion $j':X\hookrightarrow W_Y$ and a closed immersion $v:W_Y\hookrightarrow V$ such that
$$vj'=j,\qquad bv=ab',\qquad qv=q',\qquad (pa)b'=iq'.$$
The map $X\to W$ is open and scheme-theoretically dense. The maps $a,v$ are proper, $pa:W\to\overline Y$ and $q':W_Y\to Y$ are proper, and the square with horizontal maps $b',i$ and vertical maps $q',pa$ is Cartesian. Thus these maps are a Cartesian refining triangle over the supplied triangle, restricting to the identity on $X$ and $Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. No separatedness of any structure map to $k$ is required. This includes $X=\varnothing$, when $W=W_Y=\varnothing$.

proof.text: The field spectrum is Noetherian. The finite-type structure map sX gives a locally Noetherian and compact X, hence a Noetherian space. Thus every morphism out of X is quasi-compact, in particular h = j ≫ b and all the lifts used below. The finite-type map sXbar gives locally Noetherian Xbar and therefore quasi-separatedness.

Set a = h.imageι, u = h.toImage and f = a ≫ p. Use the canonical image factorization u ≫ a = h. The quasi-compact immersion h has closed image inclusion a and open, topologically dense factor u. Apply nagata_sketch_closure.1 to obtain sectionwise injectivity, retaining the full scheme-theoretic image.

Let P = pullback a b with projections m to h.image and n to V, and W = pullback f i with projections w to h.image and r to Y. The projections m and w are open by base change. Lift u and j ≫ q to j' : X → W using the given commutativity and the image factorization. Since j' ≫ w = u and w is open, j' is open and topologically dense. Its quasi-compactness follows from Noetherian X.

The equality m ≫ f = (n ≫ q) ≫ i gives a canonical lift e : P → W. Its composite with w is m, so e is open. Since n is the base change of the closed immersion a, n is closed and proper. The composite e ≫ r = n ≫ q is proper. The projection r is proper by base change of the proper f = a ≫ p, hence separated. Therefore IsProper.of_comp makes e proper. The canonical lift t : X → P satisfies t ≫ e = j', by equality on both pullback projections. Since j' is dominant, e is dominant. Its range is closed because e is proper, hence it is surjective. A surjective open immersion is an isomorphism. This is the clopen-complement argument expressed through the canonical comparison of the two pullbacks.

Define v = inv e ≫ n. It is a closed immersion and proper, by transport of the closed immersion n along an isomorphism. The inverse identities give v ≫ b = w ≫ a and v ≫ q = r. Composing j' ≫ v with the monomorphism b and using j' ≫ w = u proves j' ≫ v = j. The pullback gives w ≫ f = r ≫ i, and j' has the specified two projections. These comparison maps retain the specified identity on X and Y.

Assemble properness of a and f, openness of w, properness of r, and the canonical IsPullback witness. If X is empty, the range of the dense u is empty, whose closure is empty, so h.image is empty. The projection w then forces W to be empty as well. This proves the empty case without changing the construction.
